r1-bulk1d-ring-r16s16.card:
id: r1-bulk1d-ring-r16s16
parents:
  - v039
operation: structural_mutation
language: cuda_cpp
niche:
  mem: bulk1d
  st: direct
  grid: persistent
  launch: fused
  tile: rows16
  red: warp
  cache: stream
  spec: L
hypothesis: >-
  v039 serialises load, reduce and store inside each persistent program and never prefetches, so its outstanding
  reads per SM fall well below the ~43-64 KB B200 needs. A dedicated producer thread keeps 16 x 8 KB cp.async.bulk
  loads in flight per SM. Consumer warps release stages right after their reduction. Weights sit in shared memory.
  Read issue is therefore decoupled from compute latency at one instruction per 8 KB, which should lift
  sustained bandwidth from 5.8 to about 7 TB/s.
expected_effect:
  S:
    pct: -5
    confidence: low
  M:
    pct: -12
    confidence: low
  L:
    pct: -17
    confidence: medium
resources_sm100a:
  regs_per_thread: 32
  smem_per_cta_bytes: 180488
  threads_per_cta: 544
  ctas_per_sm: 1
  bytes_in_flight_per_sm: 131072
  launches_per_call: 1
knobs:
  TR: 16
  STAGES: 16
  consumer_warps: 16
  producer_warps: 1
  grid: num_SMs
runs_on:
  H200:
    runs: true
    representative: true
    note: "same bulk/mbarrier path (sm_90); H200 needs less in flight, so expect it to show correctness and a moderate gain, not the full B200 gain"
  A100:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "runs the plain warp-per-row fallback (no cp.async.bulk on sm_80); correctness only"
  L40S:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "fallback path; correctness only"
risks:
  - "One CTA per SM with 16 consumer warps: if per-tile consumer latency (wait, LDS, 5 shuffles, rsqrt, STG) exceeds about 520 clk at 1.5 GHz, the consumers become the bottleneck; then try 2 rows per warp with TR=32 or 8 KB tiles over 2 CTAs/SM."
  - "Direct stores from only 16 warps per SM may cap write throughput; st:bulk via smem staging is the follow-up axis."
  - "A single producer thread issues all bulk copies; issue rate is about 1 per 520 clk needed, so it should be fine, but it is unmeasured on B200."
  - "Prologue (mbarrier init and 48 KB weight bulk load, an L2 hit after the first CTA) adds to S-band fixed cost; S-band loads are all issued up front, which may offset it."
  - "180 KB of dynamic smem needs the cudaFuncSetAttribute opt-in (done once on the host); it compiles for sm_100a only via the inline-PTX paths guarded by __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900."
measure_first:
  - H200
compliance:
  single_stream: true
  no_cross_call_state: true
  fp32_math: true
  no_threads_or_fork: true
  no_precompiled_binaries: true

r2-ldg256-os-r16.card:
id: r2-ldg256-os-r16
parents:
  - g2-os-r16w8
operation: port
language: cuda_cpp
niche:
  mem: ldg256
  st: direct
  grid: oneshot
  launch: fused
  tile: rows16
  red: halfwarp
  cache: stream
  spec: all
hypothesis: >-
  This keeps g2-os-r16w8's one-shot fused grid unchanged: 16 rows per 256-thread CTA, 8 CTAs per SM and 64 KB of
  loads in flight per SM. Each half-warp lane moves 32 B per ld/st.global.v8.f32, which halves load/store
  instructions and LSU requests per byte. At B200's 36 B/clk/SM under the 1.5 GHz lock, issue overhead is the likely
  cap on the parent's 6.4 TB/s (L) and 5.7 TB/s (M). H200, A100 and L40S cannot see this: they run the float4
  fallback.
expected_effect:
  S:
    pct: -3
    confidence: low
  M:
    pct: -5
    confidence: low
  L:
    pct: -6
    confidence: low
resources_sm100a:
  regs_per_thread: 30
  smem_per_cta_bytes: 0
  threads_per_cta: 256
  ctas_per_sm: 8
  bytes_in_flight_per_sm: 65536
  launches_per_call: 1
knobs:
  ROWS: 16
  THREADS: 256
  min_blocks_per_sm: 8
  QK_USE_L2_HINT: 1
runs_on:
  H200:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "sm_90 compiles the float4 fallback (__ldcs/__stcs); use for correctness only, timing does not represent the 256-bit path"
  A100:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "float4 fallback; correctness check only"
  L40S:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "float4 fallback; correctness smoke test only"
risks:
  - "ptxas may reject .L2::cache_hint combined with .v8.f32; the compile-verified forms (L1::no_allocate.v8 / st.global.v8) are available by setting QK_USE_L2_HINT=0"
  - "__launch_bounds__(256,8) caps the kernel at 32 regs; if ptxas needs more it will spill (check LOCAL in the sm_100a compile)"
  - "per-SM bytes in flight are unchanged from the parent (64 KB), so if B200 is latency/occupancy-bound rather than issue-bound the gain may be ~0"
  - "the alignment TORCH_CHECK requires 32-B aligned buffers; the harness gives 256-B aligned buffers, but any other caller with misaligned views would error rather than run"
  - "uneven wave on the smallest workloads (768 CTAs over 148 SMs, 5-6 each), the same as the parent"
measure_first:
  - H200
compliance:
  single_stream: true
  no_cross_call_state: true
  fp32_math: true
  no_threads_or_fork: true
  no_precompiled_binaries: true

r2-ldg256-tokblk.card:
id: r2-ldg256-tokblk
parents:
  - g2-os-r16w8
operation: structural_mutation
language: cuda_cpp
niche:
  mem: ldg256
  st: direct
  grid: oneshot
  launch: fused
  tile: rows64
  red: halfwarp
  cache: default
  spec: dispatch:size
hypothesis: >-
  On B200 the parent's one-shot tile has only about 64 KB of loads in flight per SM, and it drains at every CTA
  turnover. Holding T tokens of one head per half-warp works differently: all T 256-bit loads are issued before the
  reduction, weights are reused from registers, and each byte costs half the load/store instructions. This should
  give about 128 KB in flight per SM on L and lift sustained bandwidth from 6.4 toward 7+ TB/s. H200 and A100 cannot
  show the 256-bit or bytes-in-flight effect.
expected_effect:
  S:
    pct: 0
    confidence: low
  M:
    pct: -5
    confidence: low
  L:
    pct: -8
    confidence: low
resources_sm100a:
  regs_per_thread: 56
  smem_per_cta_bytes: 0
  threads_per_cta: 256
  ctas_per_sm: 4
  bytes_in_flight_per_sm: 131072
  launches_per_call: 1
knobs:
  THREADS: 256
  T_S: 1
  T_M: 2
  T_L: 4
  MINB_S: 8
  MINB_M: 6
  MINB_L: 4
dispatch:
  - max_tokens: 600
    kernel: qk_rms_tok
    meta:
      T: 1
      minBlocks: 8
  - max_tokens: 2100
    kernel: qk_rms_tok
    meta:
      T: 2
      minBlocks: 6
  - max_tokens: 4611686018427387904
    kernel: qk_rms_tok
    meta:
      T: 4
      minBlocks: 4
runs_on:
  H200:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "arch guard compiles 2x128-bit accesses on sm_90; correctness and token-blocking signal only"
  A100:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "128-bit fallback; checks correctness and the masked T=2/4 paths (odd token counts)"
  L40S:
    runs: true
    representative: false
risks:
  - "__launch_bounds__(256,8) caps T=1 at 32 regs; if ptxas spills, raise to minBlocks 6 (check LOCAL in the sm_100a compile)"
  - "T=4 rows are 24 KB apart per half-warp (4 separate 8 KB chunks per CTA); DRAM page locality may be worse than the parent's contiguous 8 KB tile"
  - "no L2 evict_first hints on the 256-bit accesses (only the verified PTX forms are used); the parent's hints may have mattered slightly"
  - "M band at T=2 with 6 CTAs/SM: 1024 tokens give 3072 CTAs (about 3.5 waves), so a partial last wave"
  - "S path untested against the Triton parent on B200; CUDA one-shot fixed cost could differ by ±5%"
measure_first:
  - H200
compliance:
  single_stream: true
  no_cross_call_state: true
  fp32_math: true
  no_threads_or_fork: true
  no_precompiled_binaries: true

r3-cute-ldg256-os-r16.card:
id: r3-cute-ldg256-os-r16
parents:
  - g2-os-r8w4
operation: new_design
language: cute_dsl
niche:
  mem: ldg256
  st: direct
  grid: oneshot
  launch: fused
  tile: rows16
  red: halfwarp
  cache: default
  spec: all
hypothesis: >-
  The design is the parent's one-shot fused structure, but each thread moves 256-bit vectors through a CuTe DSL
  CopyUniversalOp with num_bits_per_copy=256, which Triton cannot emit. That halves the LDG/STG count per byte and
  doubles the bytes per outstanding instruction, which matters at 36 B/clk/SM at the 1.5 GHz lock. The parent sits
  at 6.4 TB/s on the L band, and this should move it toward about 7 TB/s. A single dynamic-shape compile serves all
  16 workloads.
expected_effect:
  S:
    pct: 0
    confidence: low
  M:
    pct: -3
    confidence: low
  L:
    pct: -5
    confidence: low
resources_sm100a:
  regs_per_thread: 32
  smem_per_cta_bytes: 0
  threads_per_cta: 256
  ctas_per_sm: 8
  bytes_in_flight_per_sm: 65536
  launches_per_call: 1
knobs:
  VEC: 8
  THREADS: 256
  ROWS: 16
  TPR: 16
  fallback: "VEC=4, ROWS=8, TPR=32 if the 256-bit atom fails to compile"
dispatch: []
runs_on:
  H200:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "sm_90 has no 256-bit LDG; the atom either fails (falls back to 128-bit) or splits; correctness and S-band signal only"
  A100:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "correctness smoke test; the vector width may differ from the B200 path"
  L40S:
    runs: true
    representative: false
risks:
  - "CuTe DSL 4.4.2 API details are unverified on CSF3 and may need a repair round: mark_compact_shape_dynamic stride_order, make_fragment_like naming, cute.math.rsqrt(fastmath), TensorSSA.reduce signature, a jit helper called inside a dynamic if."
  - "CopyUniversalOp with 256 bits may lower to 2 x LDG.128. That is still correct, but it brings no gain over the parent. Check the sm_100a SASS for LDG.E.ENL2.256."
  - "Without evict_first hints the L2 policy may differ slightly from the parent."
  - "The first-call compile is about 20 s, or about 40 s if the fallback triggers. It happens once, in round 0, well inside 300 s."
  - "If the CuTe DSL compiler leaves a background thread alive, the harness thread-count check would flag it. Verify on CSF3 with threading.active_count() before and after the first call."
  - "Each call builds DLPack wrappers and a CUstream on the CPU. This is host-only work and is not timed."
measure_first:
  - H200
compliance:
  single_stream: true
  no_cross_call_state: true
  fp32_math: true
  no_threads_or_fork: true
  no_precompiled_binaries: true

task.instructions: Explore the empty niche lang:cutedsl. Write the design in CuTe DSL (Python), which compiles for sm_100a; use it to reach a memory path Triton cannot express. It must be correct for every shape; aim to beat the parent somewhere and say where in the card.

r3-os-l2pf-r8w4.card:
id: r3-os-l2pf-r8w4
parents:
  - g2-os-r8w4
operation: structural_mutation
language: cuda_cpp
niche:
  mem: ldg128
  st: direct
  grid: oneshot
  launch: fused
  tile: rows8
  red: warp
  cache: stream
  spec: L
hypothesis: >-
  The one-shot parent's in-flight reads are tied to resident CTAs. CTA turnover and each CTA's own cold-DRAM wait
  therefore cost bandwidth in steady state and in the M-band tail. One cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 per CTA, two
  resident waves ahead, keeps about 10 MB of reads queued at DRAM regardless of residency. Demand loads become L2
  hits. Dynamic CTA scheduling is kept, unlike the persistent designs that all lost on B200. H200 cannot show the
  B200-specific size of this effect (36 B/clk/SM at 1.5 GHz, higher loaded latency).
expected_effect:
  S:
    pct: 0
    confidence: medium
  M:
    pct: -6
    confidence: low
  L:
    pct: -4
    confidence: low
resources_sm100a:
  regs_per_thread: 30
  smem_per_cta_bytes: 0
  threads_per_cta: 128
  ctas_per_sm: 16
  bytes_in_flight_per_sm: 131072
  launches_per_call: 1
knobs:
  ROWS: 8
  num_warps: 4
  PF_WAVES: 2
  PF_BYTES: 4096
runs_on:
  H200:
    runs: true
    representative: true
    note: "has cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2; closest proxy for the prefetch effect"
  A100:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "prefetch compiled out below sm_90; measures only the plain CUDA port"
  L40S:
    runs: true
    representative: false
    note: "prefetch compiled out below sm_90; correctness smoke test"
risks:
  - "L2 bulk prefetches may be throttled or dropped under load, giving no gain (the cost is only 1 instruction per CTA)"
  - "If DRAM efficiency (read/write mix, write-backs of the flush's dirty L2 lines) is the true limit at about 82%, more queued reads cannot help"
  - "Prefetched lines (about 10 MB in flight) could be evicted before use; then only extra request overhead, no extra DRAM bytes, since misses merge"
  - "Assumes CTAs are dispatched in roughly increasing blockIdx order; if not, part of the prefetch lead is lost"
  - "The CUDA C++ port may differ from the Triton parent's codegen (registers, scheduling); compare the A100 timing against the parent to isolate the port effect"
measure_first:
  - H200
compliance:
  single_stream: true
  no_cross_call_state: true
  fp32_math: true
  no_threads_or_fork: true
  no_precompiled_binaries: true

task.instructions: Goal: raise sustained bandwidth on medium and large inputs (B*S > 600) on B200. The parent reaches 5.75 TB/s (M) and 6.44 TB/s (L); 7.2 TB/s would add about +0.041 to the score. Propose the single change most likely to get there, correct for every shape, one launch. Slower on B200 than the parent in these bands already: g2-tma-r8s3 (tma-tensor/persistent): +16%; g2-tmaws-hb8s4 (tma-tensor/persistent-wstat): +10%; g2-ws-hb16w8s3 (cpasync/persistent-wstat): +14%; v028 (ldg128/persistent): +45%; v039 (ldg128/persistent): +12%; v040 (ldg128/oneshot): +123%; v050 (ldg128/oneshot): +26%. Ideas already proposed but not yet measured on B200 (do not repeat them): r1-bulk1d-ring-r16s16 (bulk1d/persistent, cuda_cpp); r2-ldg256-os-r16 (ldg256/oneshot, cuda_cpp); r2-ldg256-tokblk (ldg256/oneshot, cuda_cpp).

r3-tokblk-s-disp.card:
id: r3-tokblk-s-disp
parents:
  - g2-os-r8w4
operation: specialisation
language: triton
niche:
  mem: ldg128
  st: direct
  grid: oneshot
  launch: fused
  tile: rows32
  red: warp
  cache: stream
  spec: dispatch:size
hypothesis: >-
  On B200 the parent's S-band fixed cost of about 3 us is estimated to consist of:
  (1) launch plus CTA/warp ramp, about 0.5-1 us, for about 10 CTAs and 41 warps per SM, plus a partial
      second wave at B*S=256 (3,072 CTAs against 2,368 slots);
  (2) cold DRAM latency, including die crossing, about 0.8-1 us;
  (3) write-backs of the dirty L2 lines left by the flush, about 0.5-1 us, which look fixed at small sizes;
  (4) every CTA re-requesting its weight tile, which doubles L1/L2 requests and convoys on the first DRAM miss
      of the 384 weight lines;
  (5) store drain and teardown, about 0.5 us.
  The specialist attacks (1) and (4). It launches 384-396 CTAs (about 2.6 per SM, 4x fewer warps), every CTA is
  resident in one wave, each thread issues 8 independent 16-B x loads up front, and the weight tile is loaded once
  per program for 2-4 tokens. H200 cannot show the B200 ramp/latency balance at 1.5 GHz.

  S:
    pct: -12
    confidence: low
  M:
    pct: 0
    confidence: high
  L:
    pct: 0
    confidence: high

  - max_tokens: 320

    runs: true
    representative: true
    note: "closest latency structure; per-SM warp/ramp effects at 1.5 GHz are not reproduced"

risks:
  - "About 11 warps per SM may hide the reduction/store phase worse than 41 warps; it could be slower if CTA ramp was not the cost"
  - "Triton may insert a layout conversion (shared memory plus barrier) for the w[None,:,:] broadcast; check that metadata.shared == 0 in the sm_100a compile"
  - "Registers may exceed about 72 if ptxas does not fold the constant offsets; still far below the occupancy limit for this grid"
  - "Uneven CTAs per SM (2 vs 3) only matters if a per-SM issue limit binds before DRAM"
  - "B*S=586 stays on the parent (its 195 KB per SM cannot be held in registers in one wave), so the gain is limited to four workloads"
measure_first:
  - H200
compliance:
  single_stream: true
  no_cross_call_state: true
  fp32_math: true
  no_threads_or_fork: true
  no_precompiled_binaries: true

task.instructions: Goal: cut the fixed cost on small inputs (B*S <= 600). On B200 the parent fits 3.1 us fixed + bytes / 6.7 TB/s on small and medium sizes; reaching 1.5 us fixed would add about +0.026 to the score. Write a small-input kernel behind a dispatch:size wrapper that routes every larger size to the parent's kernel with the parent's exact configuration, so the B200 result isolates the change. Keep the answer focused: one candidate, and say in the card what you think the fixed cost consists of. Slower on B200 than the parent in this band already: g2-tma-r8s3 (tma-tensor/persistent): +30%; g2-tmaws-hb8s4 (tma-tensor/persistent-wstat): +16%; g2-ws-hb16w8s3 (cpasync/persistent-wstat): +6%; v028 (ldg128/persistent): +38%; v039 (ldg128/persistent): +16%; v040 (ldg128/oneshot): +70%; v050 (ldg128/oneshot): +128%. Ideas already proposed but not yet measured on B200 (do not repeat them): r1-bulk1d-ring-r16s16 (bulk1d/persistent, cuda_cpp); r2-ldg256-os-r16 (ldg256/oneshot, cuda_cpp); r2-ldg256-tokblk (ldg256/oneshot, cuda_cpp).
